text:
Alex: FYI after landing the attention-kernel v5 change on r2.14.3 we're observing elevated p99 for small microbatches on routes with high prefix cache hit rates. Not huge throughput loss but p99 +~25ms on some assistant routes.

Maria: repro steps and build? :thinking:

Alex: staging image r2.14.3, kernel v5. Seen on short prompt + long gen flows. Flame shows lots of kernel launches where previously we had fewer, larger kernels.

Jin: sounds like packing mismatch. We still pack by requested seq_len even when kv cache shaves off prefix tokens, right? so virtual compute length reduces but packing doesn't adapt.

Sasha: yes. Effectively we end up with many more tiny microbatches that hit the kernel launch path and also take the new `kv_hit` branch in v5. Branch + launch overhead dominates for these tiny sequences.

Tim: can we get kernel launch counts / occupancy from the profiler? if launch overhead is dominant, reducing launches or avoiding branch inside kernel helps.

Alex: uploaded flame: s3://redwood-perf/trace/2469001234-v5-launch-flame.svg

Maria: looked at it. v5 introduced a runtime dispatch that checks a per-request kv_hit_mask and conditionally runs different code paths. On sub-32-token effective sequences that check costs almost as much as matmul.

Jin: mitigations to consider:
- packer: coalesce requests by effective length (use kv_prefix_len to estimate)
- admission: label requests as HIT when kv_prefix_len>0 and prefer HIT+HIT packing within a short window
- token budget: increase target microbatch tokens for hit-heavy lanes so we build larger kernels

Sasha: I can add a cheap 'hit-coalesce' admission policy: mark requests with kv_prefix_len>0 as HIT and only pack HITs with each other for a 75-150ms window. Minimal codepath change in packer.

Tim: tradeoffs: this will lower latency for hit requests but may delay misses. We need sim/harness numbers before enabling on latency-SLO routes.

Alex: ran local sim (40% hits, 60% misses). With hit-coalesce=100ms: hit p99 down ~18ms, overall p95 about same, miss p99 up ~6-9ms in a skewed arrival pattern.

Maria: that looks like a reasonable opt-in for non-SLO routes. We should gate behind per-route config. Also we need telemetry to detect misclassification when cache partially matches.

Jin: longer-term we can push logic into packer/kernel boundary: emit a microbatch metadata flag (HIT vs MISS) and have two lightweight kernel variants: hit-optimized (no kv branching) and miss-optimized. Router picks kernel by microbatch flag. That avoids per-request branching at kernel entry.

Sasha: agree. That requires an ABI change between packer and kernel header (metadata word) but it's straightforward.

Tim: next steps proposed:
1) short-term: implement feature-flagged 'hit-coalesce' admission policy in packer, default off, enable in staging
2) mid-term: add microbatch metadata & two kernel variants; runtime chooses kernel by flag
3) long-term: per-route token-budget auto-tuner that raises target tokens when hit_rate exceeds threshold

Alex: I'll open a PR for (1) today: branch feature/hit-coalesce, include small sim harness snippet and dashboard query for p99-by-route + hit_rate. Will add trace metadata kv_prefix_len to help debug mismatches.

Maria: add rollback criteria in the PR description: rollback if miss p99 > +10% on route, overall error rate +5%, or GPU host CPU > baseline +15%. Include runbook steps. :thumbsup:

Jin: I'll start a prototype for the microbatch metadata path. Might need a minor kernel ABI bump; will coordinate with eng-runtime and eng-runtime-infra.

Sasha: also add a trace correlation id so we can separate true cache hits vs opportunistic heuristic labels. Saw a few false-classifications in replay traces where prefix matched partially.

deploy-bot: staging image r2.14.4-feature-hit-coalesce (build 3789) queued for deploy in 10m

Tim: thanks — let's monitor staging telemetry and meet next day to review. Keep the feature flag off in production until we have rollback thresholds satisfied.

Alex: noted, will post PR link and perf results when staging run completes.

Jin: bonus research idea: persistent kernel worker for tiny hit microbatches to amortize launch costs (like a resident kernel loop). More invasive but could cut launch overhead substantially. Marking as research spike.

Sasha: filed a short RFC in the eng-runtime workspace to capture kernel-variant and persistent-kernel ideas.

Alex: end.
